statement: No record shows that Orb has seen the menu, how-to, hint, notice or settings text: the strings list made for Orb's marks holds 1115 strings and its Mark column is empty in every row.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; the team's part is a shorter list of what a tester really meets, the rest is Orb's reading time
risk: Outside testers read text that Orb's own rule says must be seen first; known early by an unmarked list at the candidate.
orb_question: Will you mark a short list (the notice, the start menu, the how-to card, the match-over card, the report panel) before outside testers play? Recommendation: yes, a cut-down list of about 150 strings, not all 1115.

statement: The fighters say nothing in a match: the approved lines are switched off on main and in the build Orb last played, and the switch table has no row for them.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; the emitter and the 355 lines exist, the work is one switch, a caption fit check at 1280 by 800 and a play check
risk: The emitter is said to read events only and never write the sim (live_barks.json:3); that was not run here, so a golden check must confirm it.
orb_question: Should Grist and Loupe speak their approved lines in the Alpha? Recommendation: yes, switched on in the tester build once the captions are checked on the Deck's screen.

statement: The line check for fighter lines is run by hand only: no CI job names it and no saved result exists for the baseline.
risk: A later edit to the lines could break Orb's rules unseen.

statement: The how-to card names keyboard keys to a pad player: its corner hint reads "Enter: next   Esc: close" whenever touch is off, and its reopen line says "the pause menu or F1".
risk: A Deck tester with no keyboard is told to press keys they do not have.

statement: The title is shown and stamped as plain "Orb Combat EX" with no working-title mark, while Legal's page says the visible heading may keep "(working title)" until the search is done.
orb_question: Should the Alpha build show "(working title)" beside the name? Recommendation: yes, on the start menu and the tester note only, until the title search is done.

statement: The placeholder names KAI and VORR remain in data and code a player does not see: a placeholder line file no game code reads, a note in the recipes data, an effects list and the JS reference core.
risk: The translation string tool reads the placeholder file, so placeholder lines could enter a string list for translators.

statement: Words for the backburnered meters and for hiding are still in the player-facing word list, and the F2 key swaps in the old greybox HUD that draws MENACE and ANGUISH bars.
risk: A tester with a keyboard can reach words for systems Orb set aside.

statement: The check that no player-facing text says KAI or VORR lives in a hand-run HUD check that no CI job runs, and no saved run of it exists for the baseline.

A few how-to lines are not plain or not true for a desktop tester: the planet bar is called "the strip", the rival is "his", and the privacy line speaks of a web version and a clipboard, not of the report folder.
The fighters' names come from one data file (Grist, Loupe) and the UI swaps roster ids for them; no file in ui/data contains KAI or VORR.

All 355 fighter lines in the live file carry a source that traces to Orb (own words, kept, or reviewed rewrites), 237 of them for the two Alpha fighters, with no banned word and every length break either Orb's own words or waived by id.
The how-to card and hints are data, written in short plain sentences, with the AI disclosure on the About page and the music and voice lines hidden while their flags are off.
The flashing-effects notice text exists as data and is the first batch in the strings list.
